note: Tonight's contacts (scripts/core/shift_state.gd draws them; scripts/ui/clipboard.gd prints the list). Written by the assistant on 2026-11-17 for the student's story notes: the doctor fronts a Lantern street clinic, and some visitors are Lantern couriers carrying contraband chrome. Each night rules.json contacts.per_night entries are drawn, each for a different visitor of that night. An entry never names its courier: it gives an alias and two clues, and only the two clues together point at one visitor. case_db checks the list as written against the roster (every clue fits at least two people, every entry's two clues fit its own courier), and since who comes in is drawn (rules.json night, version 9), each night keeps only the entries that are fair among that night's visitors (case_db fair_contacts): each clue alone fits at least two of them, and the two together fit the courier and nobody else who comes in. The draw makes sure at least contacts.per_night of them are left. The player matches the clues to the intake card (age, fee, request) and to what the eyes look like, then clicks SAY. The right courier answers with the entry's answer line and hands over the package (rules.json contacts.pay). Any other visitor, or the wrong code to a courier, gets that visitor's own lines.code and costs contacts.wrong_cost patience, so a wrong code says nothing about who is a courier. Codes are game-owned: no model call is made and nothing is added to the patient's history. Numbers live in rules.json; only words and clue predicates live here. On screen a visitor on the list is always a contact, never a courier, because Kip's own job is bike courier; the code and the tests still say courier for the role. Nobody has playtested them.
